summary: In this fiction excerpt from a novel's Book 3, the narrator watches Alex Goddard, posing as a scientist, perform an in vitro-style embryo implantation on a sedated woman while Marcelina runs an ultrasound. The narrator links the procedure to Sarah's earlier 'hallucinations' of a green mask and a long white tunnel, fears being drugged and taken, and wonders what the hidden computers hold. Marcelina then announces the narrator's room is ready and offers to wash her things, prompting the narrator to demand answers about what happened to Sarah.
one_line: The narrator watches Alex Goddard implant embryos in a sedated woman, suspects Sarah was similarly treated, and confronts Marcelina.
key_facts: Alex Goddard removes three glass ampules of frozen embryos from a tube and places them in a container before the implantation.
Marcelina operates an ultrasound scanner over the woman's stomach, showing her uterus and Fallopian tubes on the screen above the table.
Alex Goddard inserts a needle into the woman's abdomen while watching the ultrasound, and all three embryos are implanted.
The narrator describes Alex Goddard's implantation as performed with 'flawless precision it was scary.'
The narrator recalls Sarah mentioning a green mask and a sinister event that felt like disappearing down a long white tunnel.
The narrator asks whether Sarah was given an in vitro procedure too, and whether her experience was her own anesthesia.
The operating table is rolled out of the OR and back down the hall with a 'bump, thump, bump' sound.
The narrator switches off the monitor and turns to stare at the computers, asking why they are in this 'place of miracles.'
Marcelina opens the office door and says, 'Your room is ready now,' with heavily accented but sure English.
Marcelina offers to wash any of the narrator's things.
The narrator has not checked in and is surprised by the room arrangement.
The narrator plans to ask Marcelina what happened to Sarah the last time she was there and whether Sarah was operated on the same way.
The narrator also wants to ask why the woman was so taken in by Alex Goddard's 'phony Mardi Gras mysticism.'
